author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Resolver locations are parsed with URL before raw dot-segment rejection, so reader, author, and PDF targets can be accepted after path normalization.
findings.consequence: A malformed resolver response such as /författare/A/../B/dramawebben or /txt/a/../b/b.pdf is silently converted into a different accepted redirect target instead of being treated as an unavailable resolver response. This weakens the response-boundary check and can hide backend contract bugs; the information-location branch already has stricter raw-path checks, but the other accepted shapes do not.
findings.evidence: parseLocalLocation constructs new URL(value, ...) on line 92 and returns decoded segments from the normalized URL pathname. A read-only Node URL probe showed /författare/A/../B/dramawebben normalizes to /f%C3%B6rfattare/B/dramawebben, which then matches isAuthorLocation. The SSR tests include normalized traversal rejection only for information URLs, not for reader, author, or PDF resolver locations.
findings.recommendation: Reject raw path dot segments before URL normalization, or decode and validate the rawPathname segments directly for all accepted resolver-location shapes rather than deriving structural segments from URL.pathname.
